title: Challenge: triage and roll back a bad deploy
intro: 3 a.m. page: the 'api' deployment is down after a release. Triage it like an SRE, find the failure, confirm the cause, and roll back to the last good version. (Commands checked; output illustrative.)

steps.instruction: Start with the blast radius: list the pods for the api.
steps.success:
NAME                   READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
api-7d9f8c6b5-abc12    0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          3m   <- not healthy

steps.instruction: Find out WHY it's crashing: read the logs of the crashing pod.
steps.success:
Error: cannot connect to database: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db-prod
  the new release points at a hostname that doesn't exist
steps.hint: kubectl logs api-7d9f8c6b5-abc12   (add --previous if it already restarted)

steps.instruction: It's a bad release. Check the deployment's rollout history to see the revisions.
steps.success:
deployment.apps/api
REVISION  CHANGE-CAUSE
1         good release
2         broke db host   <- current
steps.fail: Show the rollout history of the api deployment.

steps.instruction: Roll back to the previous, working revision, stop the bleeding first, debug later.
steps.fail: Undo the rollout on the api deployment.

steps.instruction: Confirm recovery: list the pods again.
steps.success:
NAME                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
api-5c4b3a2f1-z9y8x    1/1     Running   0          12s   <- healthy again
steps.fail: List the pods to confirm they're Running.

done: Solved! Triage order matters: assess (get pods) → diagnose (logs) → mitigate (rollback) → confirm. Restore service first; write the postmortem after.
